correctness.rationale: Any selected pair at underlying cyclic distance 2..2r has an outside-or-selected common neighbor on a shortest arc, forcing a closer selected pair under threshold-two convex closure, ultimately adjacent cyclic vertices; r>=2 then forces both outer neighbors repeatedly and hence the full cycle. Conversely, separated selected pairs have distance >2r, so any outside vertex cannot have two selected neighbors by metric triangle inequality. Ordering k>=2 selected points around labelled C_n gives all positive gaps >=2r+1, with weak compositions and n/k unmarking giving the binomial coefficient. n small and complete powers correctly give only empty/singleton/full; r=1 has a C7 counterexample. Independently enumerated all subsets n3..18 selected radii and matched adjacency definition and polynomial; proof is universal.

final_claim: For every n>=3,r>=2, all proper ordinary P3-convex sets of C_n^r are exactly cyclic (2r+1)-packings; full size polynomial has coefficient n/k*binom(n−2rk−1,k−1) for k>=2 and separate full-set monomial.
limitations: r>=2 only, labelled simple cycles, ordinary not induced P3 convexity; automorphism quotient or general circular-arc graphs not studied.
